methods.name: expression
methods.summary: Returns the expression in which the binding was defined (e.g. for the binding `x` in `y = (x := 1)`, return the node representing `x := 1`).

methods.name: in_assert_statement
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] took place inside an `assert` statement, e.g. `y` in: ```python assert (y := x**2), y ```

methods.name: in_exception_handler
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] took place inside an exception handler, e.g. `y` in: ```python try:      x = 42 except RuntimeError:      y = 42 ```

methods.name: is_alias
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an aliased symbol (e.g., `app` in `from fastapi import FastAPI as app`).

methods.name: is_annotated_type_alias
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents a [PEP 613] type alias e.g. `OptString` in: ```python from typing import TypeAlias

methods.name: is_deferred_type_alias
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents a [PEP 695] type alias e.g. `OptString` in: ```python type OptString = str | None ```

methods.name: is_deleted
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] was deleted.

methods.name: is_explicit_export
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an explicit re-export (e.g., `FastAPI` in `from fastapi import FastAPI as FastAPI`).

methods.name: is_external
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an external symbol (e.g., `FastAPI` in `from fastapi import FastAPI`).

methods.name: is_global
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents a `global`. A [`Binding`] is a `global` if it's declared by a `global` statement, or shadows a [`Binding`] declared by a `global` statement.

methods.name: is_invalid_all_format
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an assignment to `__all__` with an invalid value (e.g., `__all__ = "Foo"`).

methods.name: is_invalid_all_object
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an assignment to `__all__` that includes an invalid member (e.g., `__all__ = ["Foo", 1]`).

methods.name: is_nonlocal
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents a `nonlocal`. A [`Binding`] is a `nonlocal` if it's declared by a `nonlocal` statement, or shadows a [`Binding`] declared by a `nonlocal` statement.

methods.name: is_private_declaration
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an private declaration (e.g., `_x` in `_x = "private variable"`)

methods.name: is_type_alias
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents either kind of type alias

methods.name: is_unbound
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an unbound variable (e.g., `x` in `x = 1; del x`).

methods.name: is_unpacked_assignment
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] represents an unpacked assignment (e.g., `x` in `(x, y) = 1, 2`).

methods.name: is_unused
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] is unused.

methods.name: is_used
methods.summary: Return `true` if this [`Binding`] is used.

methods.name: name
methods.summary: Returns the name of the binding (e.g., `x` in `x = 1`).

methods.name: parent_range
methods.summary: Returns the range of the binding's parent.

methods.name: redefines
methods.summary: Return `true` if this binding "redefines" the given binding, as per Pyflake's definition of redefinition.

methods.name: references
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over all references for the current [`Binding`].

methods.name: statement
methods.summary: Returns the statement in which the binding was defined.

items.name: FromImport
items.summary: A binding for a member imported from a module, keyed on the name to which the member is bound. Ex) `from foo import bar` would be keyed on "bar". Ex) `from foo import bar as baz` would be keyed on "baz".

methods.name: member_name
methods.summary: For example, given `from foo import bar`, returns `"bar"`.

methods.name: module_name
methods.summary: For example, given `from foo import bar`, returns `["foo"]`.

methods.name: qualified_name
methods.summary: For example, given `from foo import bar`, returns `["foo", "bar"]`.

items.name: Import
items.summary: A binding for an `import`, keyed on the name to which the import is bound. Ex) `import foo` would be keyed on "foo". Ex) `import foo as bar` would be keyed on "bar".

methods.name: member_name
methods.summary: For example, given `import foo`, returns `"foo"`.

methods.name: module_name
methods.summary: For example, given `import foo`, returns `["foo"]`.

methods.name: qualified_name
methods.summary: For example, given `import foo`, returns `["foo"]`.

items.name: SubmoduleImport
items.summary: A binding for a submodule imported from a module, keyed on the name of the parent module. Ex) `import foo.bar` would be keyed on "foo".

methods.name: member_name
methods.summary: For example, given `import foo.bar`, returns `"foo.bar"`.

methods.name: module_name
methods.summary: For example, given `import foo.bar`, returns `["foo"]`.

methods.name: qualified_name
methods.summary: For example, given `import foo.bar`, returns `["foo", "bar"]`.

methods.name: member_name
methods.summary: Returns the member name of the imported symbol. For a straight import, this is equivalent to the qualified name; for a `from` import, this is the name of the imported symbol.

methods.name: module_name
methods.summary: Returns the module name of the imported symbol.

methods.name: qualified_name
methods.summary: Returns the call path to the imported symbol.

methods.name: source_name
methods.summary: Returns the source module of the imported symbol.
